references.text: This passage establishes circumcision as a sign of the covenant between God and Abraham's descendants, specifying that it must occur on the eighth day – something Abraham now fulfills through Isaac's circumcision.
God specifically commanded that every male child be circumcised when eight days old, which Abraham obeys here by circumcising Isaac.
The Mosaic law confirms the command for circumcision on the eighth day, first given to Abraham and practiced in Isaac's circumcision.
Jesus was circumcised on the eighth day in accordance with the same command that Abraham followed when he circumcised Isaac.
Stephen refers to the covenant of circumcision God made with Abraham, noting that Abraham circumcised Isaac on the eighth day.
Distinguishes between Isaac's specific covenantal circumcision on the 8th day and the simultaneous circumcision of Ishmael and his household.
A complementary account placing Isaac's circumcision in the timeline alongside the circumcisions of Abraham and Ishmael.
Contrasts Abraham's initiation into the covenant (at age 99) with Isaac's continuation of the covenant (at 8 days old).
Highlights the theological significance of Isaac's circumcision as a sign that Abraham is the father of both the circumcised and those who believe.
Explains the theological meaning of circumcision as a 'seal' of righteousness by faith, which forms the basis for Isaac's circumcision.
